sentence: There isn't ______ milk in the fridge.
explanation: 'Much' se usa con sustantivos <uncountable> en oraciones negativas y preguntas.
tip: Milk is uncountable — which quantifier works with uncountable nouns in negatives?

sentence: How ______ books do you have?
explanation: 'Many' se usa con sustantivos <countable> plurales en preguntas y negaciones.
tip: Books are countable — which quantifier do we use with countable nouns?

sentence: I have ______ friends in this city.
explanation: 'Some' se usa en oraciones <positive> tanto con sustantivos contables como incontables.
tip: Positive sentence + plural noun = 'some' (an unspecified number).

sentence: Is there ______ sugar in the cupboard?
explanation: 'Any' se usa en <questions> tanto con sustantivos contables como incontables.
tip: This is a question — which word replaces 'some' in questions?

sentence: She doesn't have ______ time today.
explanation: 'Much' se usa con sustantivos incontables en negaciones. Time es incontable.
tip: Negative + uncountable (time) — which quantifier?

sentence: There are ______ people waiting outside.
explanation: 'A lot of' funciona tanto con sustantivos contables como incontables en oraciones afirmativas.
tip: Positive sentence, many people — 'a lot of' is the most natural choice.

sentence: He doesn't have ______ experience.
explanation: 'Much' se usa con sustantivos incontables en negaciones. Experience es incontable.
tip: Negative + uncountable = 'much'.

sentence: Would you like ______ water?
explanation: 'Some' se usa en ofrecimientos y peticiones (aunque sean preguntas).
tip: Offers use 'some' even in question form — we expect 'yes'.

sentence: I didn't buy ______ eggs at the shop.
explanation: 'Any' se usa en oraciones <negative> con sustantivos contables e incontables.
tip: Negative + countable plural = 'any' (zero quantity).

sentence: There is very ______ water left in the bottle.
explanation: 'Little' (no mucho) se usa con sustantivos <uncountable> para expresar 'no suficiente'.
tip: Uncountable + 'not enough' = 'little'. With 'very' it emphasizes scarcity.

sentence: ______ students passed the exam — only three.
explanation: 'Few' (no muchos) se usa con sustantivos <countable> plurales para expresar 'no suficiente'.
tip: Countable + 'not many' = 'few'. Only three = a small number.

sentence: I need ______ help with this exercise.
explanation: 'Some' en una oración afirmativa con un sustantivo incontable (help).
tip: Positive statement asking for an unspecified amount of help.

sentence: How ______ money do you need?
explanation: 'How much' se usa con sustantivos incontables (money). 'How many' con sustantivos contables.
tip: Money is uncountable — 'how much' or 'how many'?

sentence: There are a ______ good restaurants near here.
explanation: 'A few' (algunos, suficientes) con sustantivos contables plurales. Sentido afirmativo.
tip: 'A few' = some, it's positive. 'Few' (without 'a') = not enough.

sentence: She has ______ patience with rude people.
explanation: 'Little' con sustantivos incontables = no mucho / no suficiente.
tip: Patience is uncountable. She doesn't have enough → 'little'.

sentence: There aren't ______ oranges left in the basket.
explanation: 'Many' se usa con sustantivos <countable> plurales en negaciones. 'Oranges' es contable.
tip: Oranges are countable and this is negative — 'many' or 'much'?

sentence: We don't need ______ sugar for this recipe.
explanation: 'Much' se usa con sustantivos incontables en negaciones. 'Sugar' es incontable.
tip: Sugar is uncountable — negative sentence needs 'much'.

sentence: There were ______ people at the concert — it was packed.
explanation: 'A lot of' funciona con sustantivos contables e incontables en oraciones afirmativas.
tip: Positive sentence, many people — use 'a lot of'.

sentence: I have ______ time to finish this today, so let's hurry.
explanation: 'Little' (no mucho) se usa con incontables para expresar escasez. 'Time' es incontable.
tip: Uncountable + not enough = 'little'.

sentence: ______ tourists visit this town — it's not very popular.
explanation: 'Few' (no muchos) se usa con contables plurales para expresar escasez.
tip: Countable + not enough = 'few'.
